findings.description: The auto-delete test runs `git push origin --delete` from the clone, and that push also drops the clone's `refs/remotes/origin/feature/autodeleted`. So the test never hits the case its comment describes: a forge deletes the branch while the clone still holds a stale tracking ref. To cover that case, delete the branch on the bare origin directly (`update-ref -d`, as the race test does) and assert stderr has no "delete refused". Otherwise, dropping `--prune` from the fetch would still pass this test.

process_issues.description: `.claude-pr/` held only `.claude` and `CLAUDE.md`. The workflow's `RESTORE_PATHS` entries (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents`, `templates`) were not snapshotted there, even though the restore step copies each one into `.claude-pr/$path` before taking the base copy. Reviewers read the PR's `templates/agents/scripts/worktree-remove.sh` and `.agents/worktree.env` with `git show HEAD:<path>` and `gh pr diff` instead, so coverage was not lost. Check whether the action's own restore wipes or recreates `.claude-pr/` after the workflow step runs.

Only correctness, conventions and docs ran. Security was skipped because the change crosses no trust boundary. Context was skipped because no spec, protocol or CI-workflow surface changed beyond a packaging smoke assertion. Maintainability was skipped because the logic change is one refspec line.
